name: n8n: Dockerized self-host stack
description: Self-hosted n8n automation with Docker Compose, backup scripts, and proxy-oriented layout for secrets, network exposure, and repeatable operations.
longDescription: Self-hosted workflow automation using Docker Compose: service definitions, scripts, and supporting assets to run n8n on private infrastructure. Backup scripts and deployment directories keep secrets, TLS material, and internal endpoints out of published source trees. The layout emphasises repeatable start, stop, backup, and upgrade operations while keeping business workflow logic decoupled from infrastructure code.
features: Compose-first layout for controlled automation hosting
Backup script scaffolding for database snapshots
Separation between runtime volumes, versioned config, and secret env files
Proxy and TLS material folders populated per operator
Documented network posture: reverse proxy and firewall over broad port exposure
highlights: Keeps workflow automation under your own container runtime
Secrets and hostnames stay in private configuration only
challenges: Self-hosted automation must stay patched, backed up, and reachable only to trusted networks.
solutions: Compose with documented volumes, scripted backups, and TLS termination at the edge proxy.
security: Store webhook URLs, API keys, and database passwords only in private env files
Restrict administrative ports via firewall or VPN
Rotate automation credentials on a schedule
Least privilege for service accounts reaching webhooks and databases
